transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (CSM), Carlos (Redwood SE), Ellen (Blue Nimbus VP Eng), Marcus (Blue Nimbus SRE), Nia (PM)

Summary:
Quick activation kickoff to align network, access, and success metrics for Blue Nimbus's pilot. Main topics: VPC/on-prem connectivity questions, observability/trace retention, expected latency SLAs, and pilot workload definition. Agreed next steps and owners at end.

Topics:
- Access & network (VPC CIDR, peering, firewall)
- Security artifacts (SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs)
- Runtime profile & perf targets (p99 latency, throughput)
- Staging access and bench plan
- Success milestones and weekly cadence

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, im Jordan Ellis AE, I'm with Priya and Carlos from our side. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Ellen: Hey Jordan, doing well. Thanks for setting this up. We just want to make sure we can hit internal timelines, kind of a tight pilot window.
[00:18] Priya: Hi Ellen, hi Marcus, thanks for the time. We'll keep this practical — network, security, and the execution plan.
[00:25] Marcus: Quick context — we run most services in a VPC on AWS, we have a corporate proxy and strict egress rules, and our security team needs to sign off on any external endpoints.
[00:36] Carlos: Got it. We'll walk through the connectivity options — good news is Redwood supports Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private in-VPC deployment. For this pilot do you expect to use our Private VPC offering or start with Hosted and then move?
[00:48] Nia: We were thinking Private if possible. The product team wants consistent latency and no data egress.
[00:54] Ellen: Sizing is also a question — we have conversational support and some reranking jobs. We're not large traffic, but we care about p99 latency under 300ms for short chats.
[01:06] Jordan: That's helpful — p99 300ms is a reasonable target for a trimmed context length and batching. We'll need sample prompts and typical sequence lengths to validate. Carlos, feel free to add.
[01:16] Carlos: Yeah, two things — first, we recommend a sandbox staging project so you can test with your CIDR and proxy. Second, caching is usually our biggest win — prefix/K V cash (transcription glitch: K V cash) — i mean KV cache for repeated prompts which dramatically lowers latency.
[01:35] Marcus: The caching piece is interesting, we have session affinity at the LB level, would that play well with your KV caching?
[01:42] Carlos: We can route by policy; session affinity is fine. We'll map how the runtime pins KV cache to instances. There may be a need to run a small dedicated pool if you want guaranteed warm caches.
[01:55] Ellen: Security — we need SOC2 artifacts, SSO through SAML, and KMS/HSM key controls. Also we have data residency constraints for EU customers, is that something you support?
[02:07] Priya: Yes, we can provide SOC2 and ISO artifacts; SAML SSO is supported and KMS integrations are available for Private deployments. For data residency, we can pin region or do on-prem for stricter controls.
[02:20] Nia: Timeline wise — we want to run a two-week pilot starting mid-June, with benchmarks in first week and a user trial second week.
[02:29] Jordan: That sounds doable. Let's capture milestone dates in the success plan. Priya will send a 60/90/120 day plan after this call.
[02:37] Marcus: Firewalls — we need to share our egress IPs or peering info. Do you allow VPC peering or only private link type?
[02:46] Carlos: For Redwood Private in-VPC, we typically do a managed control plane with your VPC peered for control signals and the data plane runs in customer-managed subnets; peering or Transit Gateway are both options. For Hosted API there are fixed egress IPs but that route requires an allowlist and has more scrutiny.
[03:04] Ellen: Okay send over the diagram.
[03:06] Jordan: Will do, we'll include a diagram and an onboarding runbook link in the follow-up.
[03:10] Nia: Observability — what telemetry do we get? We need traces per request and token-level cost breakdown for our finance folks.
[03:20] Priya: Console provides per-route token breakdowns, latency histograms, and tracing hooks you can integrate with Jaeger or Datadog. We also have event logs and audit trails for token-level visibility.
[03:32] Marcus: Retention — what's the default retention on logs? We need 13 months for audit.
[03:37] Priya: Out of the box it's shorter, but enterprise add-on can extend retention and export to your S3 or SIEM. We'll include that in the security pack.
[03:47] Ellen: Cost — curious about the unit economics if we do Dedicated vs Hosted. Any back-of-envelope numbers?
[03:54] Jordan: We can share a cost model. Generally Dedicated gives predictable throughput and is often cheaper per token at scale, Hosted is easiest to start. For pilot scale, Hosted is usually fine and we can recommend quantization profiles and batching to lower cost.
[04:11] Carlos: Also worth noting, for latency-sensitive workloads quantization may trade a bit on quality; we'll recommend a profile after we see your evals.
[04:20] Marcus: On the SSO side — we use Okta; we'll need SAML metadata and a test user.
[04:27] Priya: We'll provide SAML examples. Jordan, can you attach SAML metadata to the follow-up?
[04:31] Jordan: Yep, will include.
[04:33] [05:00] Ellen: Anything else on integrations? We have internal tooling that will call the API from an internal service mesh. We'll need support for mTLS and internal cert pinning.
[05:12] Carlos: mTLS can be accommodated in private deployments; for Hosted we rely on TLS and allowlist. We'll flag this for architecture review.
[05:22] Nia: Pilot success criteria — what should we define?
[05:25] Priya: Typically: 1) p99 latency under agreed target for X% of calls, 2) functional parity on a sample prompt set (we'll help with evals), 3) security sign-off (SAML, KMS), and 4) deployment runbook validated.
[05:40] Ellen: That aligns. We'll add internal acceptance for UX quality and cost threshold.
[05:46] Marcus: For the bench test are you expecting us to provision load generators or do you run them?
[05:52] Carlos: We can run bench from our side against the staging project you provide. We'll share a load plan but would prefer your SRE to execute in your environment for the most realistic network path.
[06:05] [10:12] Jordan: Quick note — we'll share a short checklist: network CIDR, SAML metadata, contact for security, and sample prompts. If you can get those to us by Friday we'll aim for staging access early next week.
[10:25] Ellen: Sounds good. One more question — do you support region failover or multi-region RW setups?
[10:32] Carlos: Yes, we can blueprint multi-region, but for pilot we recommend single region with a fallback policy to a different model variant if capacity spikes. For true multi-region replication that's a longer setup.
[10:44] Nia: Good to know.
[10:47] [22:00] Marcus: On credentials, how are API keys managed? We need rotation and RBAC.
[22:06] Priya: API keys are scoped by project and we support token rotation policies. For Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and role-based access controls. We'll propose a role matrix in the runbook.
[22:18] Ellen: Are there any compliance questionnaires we'll need to fill out?
[22:22] Jordan: Yes we have an initial security questionnaire and a SOC2 package. We'll send both, and the security team can live-sync with Priya if needed.
[22:32] [33:10] Carlos: A technical caveat — if you plan long context lengths for reranking, the kernel selection becomes important; we may suggest a model variant and quantize differently. We'll include recommended profiles in the bench plan.
[33:25] Marcus: We'll share sample token distributions.
[33:29] Priya: Great — I'll add that to the success plan.
[33:33] Nia: Any blockers from your side we should be aware of?
[33:36] Jordan: None other than getting the network details and sample prompts. Also a test user for SAML will unblock SSO setup.
[33:45] Ellen: We'll get those items to you by Thursday/Friday.
[33:50] [44:00] Jordan: Final recap: Jordan to send VPC diagram + onboarding runbook; Priya will share the success plan and SAML examples; Carlos will prepare bench test config; Marcus/Ellen will provide CIDRs, proxy info, and sample prompts. We'll meet again next Tuesday for bench kickoff, does that work?
[44:20] Marcus: Yes Tuesday works for the SRE team.
[44:25] Nia: We'll lock time after the runbook arrives.
[44:30] Priya: I'll calendar a 30-minute bench sync for next week.
[44:35] Ellen: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to it.
[44:40] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts shortly.
[44:45] [54:00] End of recording.
